tree.heading: In general
tree.text: After notice and opportunity to submit comment in accordance with section 553(c) of title 5, the Board, jointly with the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection, shall prescribe regulations—

children.text: to carry out the provisions of this chapter;
to prevent the circumvention or evasion of such provisions; and
to facilitate compliance with such provisions.

tree.heading: Regulations relating to improvement of check processing system
tree.text: In order to improve the check processing system, the Board shall consider (among other proposals) requiring, by regulation, that—

children.text: depository institutions be charged based upon notification that a check or similar instrument will be presented for payment;
the Federal Reserve banks and depository institutions provide for check truncation;
depository institutions be provided incentives to return items promptly to the depository institution of first deposit;
the Federal Reserve banks and depository institutions take such actions as are necessary to automate the process of returning unpaid checks;
each depository institution and Federal Reserve bank—
place its endorsement, and other notations specified in regulations of the Board, on checks in the positions specified in such regulations; and
take such actions as are necessary to—
automate the process of reading endorsements; and
eliminate unnecessary endorsements;
within one business day after an originating depository institution is presented a check (for more than such minimum amount as the Board may prescribe)—
such originating depository institution determines whether it will pay such check; and

if such originating depository institution determines that it will not pay such check, such originating depository institution directly notify the receiving depository institution of such determination;
regardless of where a check is cleared initially, all returned checks be eligible to be returned through the Federal Reserve System;

Federal Reserve banks and depository institutions participate in the development and implementation of an electronic clearinghouse process to the extent the Board determines, pursuant to the study under subsection (f), that such a process is feasible; and
originating depository institutions be permitted to return unpaid checks directly to, and obtain reimbursement for such checks directly from, the receiving depository institution.

tree.heading: Regulatory responsibility of Board for payment system

children.heading: Responsibility for payment system
children.text: In order to carry out the provisions of this chapter, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System shall have the responsibility to regulate—
any aspect of the payment system, including the receipt, payment, collection, or clearing of checks; and
any related function of the payment system with respect to checks.

children.heading: Regulations
children.text: The Board shall prescribe such regulations as it may determine to be appropriate to carry out its responsibility under paragraph (1).

children.heading: Required reports
children.text: The Board shall transmit a report to both Houses of the Congress not later than 18, 30, and 48 months after August 10, 1987.

children.heading: Contents of report
children.text: Each such report shall describe—
the actions taken and progress made by the Board to implement the schedules established in section 4002 of this title, and
the impact of this chapter on consumers and depository institutions.

children.heading: Report required
children.text: The Board shall transmit a report to both Houses of the Congress not later than 2 years after August 10, 1987, regarding the effects the temporary schedule established under section 4002(c) of this title have had on depository institutions and the public.

children.heading: Contents of report
children.text: Such report shall also assess the potential impact the implementation of the schedule established in section 4002(b) of this title will have on depository institutions and the public, including an estimate of the risks to and losses of depository institutions and the benefits to consumers. Such report shall also contain such recommendations for legislative or administrative action as the Board may determine to be necessary.

children.heading: Comptroller General evaluation report
children.text: Not later than 6 months after September 1, 1988, the Comptroller General of the United States shall transmit a report to the Congress evaluating the implementation and administration of this chapter.

tree.heading: Consultations
tree.text: In prescribing regulations under subsections (a) and (b), the Board and the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection, in the case of subsection (a), and the Board, in the case of subsection (b), shall consult with the Comptroller of the Currency, the Board of Directors of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and the National Credit Union Administration Board.

children.heading: Study required
children.text: The Board shall study the feasibility of modernizing and accelerating the check payment system through the development of an electronic clearinghouse process utilizing existing telecommunications technology to avoid the necessity of actual presentment of the paper instrument to a payor institution before such institution is charged for the item.

children.heading: Consultation; factors to be studied
children.text: In connection with the study required under paragraph (1), the Board shall—
consult with appropriate experts in telecommunications technology; and
consider all practical and legal impediments to the development of an electronic clearinghouse process.

children.heading: Report required
children.text: The Board shall report its conclusions to the Congress within 9 months of August 10, 1987.

notes.heading: Codification
notes.text: In subsec. (d)(3), “September 1, 1988” substituted for “section 603(b) takes effect” on authority of section 613(b) of Pub. L. 100–86, set out as an Effective Date note under section 4001 of this title.

notes.heading: Amendments
notes.text: 2010—Subsec. (a). Pub. L. 111–203, § 1086(d)(1), inserted “, jointly with the Director of the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection,” after “Board” in introductory provisions. Subsec. (e). Pub. L. 111–203, § 1086(d)(2), added subsec. (e) and struck out former subsec. (e). Prior to amendment, text read as follows: “In prescribing regulations under subsections (a) and (b) of this section, the Board shall consult with the Comptroller of the Currency, the Board of Directors of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Home Loan Bank Board, and the National Credit Union Administration Board.”

notes.heading: Effective Date of 2010 Amendment
notes.text: Amendment by Pub. L. 111–203 effective on the designated transfer date, see section 1100H of Pub. L. 111–203, set out as a note under section 552a of Title 5, Government Organization and Employees.
